name: Flysta
overview: Flysta is a modern Transportation Management System designed to simplify logistics operations and help transport businesses manage their workflow through a single scalable platform.
mission: Digitize logistics workflows while providing a fast, intuitive, and maintainable enterprise experience.
problem: Transport businesses rely on manual paperwork, disconnected tools, and fragmented workflows to manage logistics operations. This leads to operational inefficiencies, data loss, and poor visibility into the supply chain.
solution: Flysta provides a unified dashboard for managing the entire logistics lifecycle — from LR creation to POD delivery — with role-based access, real-time tracking, and comprehensive reporting.
architecture: Scalable enterprise architecture with modular React frontend, RESTful API backend, and relational database design optimized for logistics workflows.
challenges: Designing a data model that accommodates complex logistics relationships
Building a responsive dashboard with real-time data updates
Implementing role-based access across multiple organizational levels
engineeringDecisions: Chose PostgreSQL for relational integrity across logistics entities
Modular component architecture for enterprise scalability
JWT-based authentication for secure multi-tenant access
lessonsLearned: Enterprise software requires deep domain understanding
Data modeling is critical for logistics applications
Role-based access must be designed from the start

name: Forgeo
overview: Forgeo is a developer growth platform that helps programmers become real software engineers. Instead of teaching through tutorials, it teaches through real-world missions and engineering thinking.
mission: Help developers think like engineers instead of simply following tutorials.
problem: Most programming education focuses on syntax and tutorials rather than engineering thinking. Developers struggle to transition from writing code to building systems.
solution: Forgeo provides mission-based learning paths that simulate real engineering challenges. Developers learn by solving problems, designing solutions, and reflecting on their approach.
architecture: Modern full-stack architecture with a focus on interactive learning experiences and personalized learning paths.
challenges: Designing missions that accurately simulate real engineering problems
Creating objective assessments for engineering thinking
Building a recommendation system for personalized learning paths
engineeringDecisions: Mission-based architecture over traditional course structure
Focus on problem-solving over content consumption
Progressive difficulty scaling aligned with real-world complexity
lessonsLearned: Teaching engineering thinking requires a different approach than teaching syntax
Interactive challenges drive deeper learning than passive content
Feedback loops are essential for skill development

name: NutriLab
overview: NutriLab is a comprehensive healthcare SaaS platform designed for nutritionists and dietitians to manage their clinics digitally.
mission: Replace manual clinic operations with a secure, scalable, production-ready digital platform.
problem: Nutritionists and dietitians manage patient records, appointments, meal plans, and prescriptions manually or through disconnected tools. This creates inefficiencies, data inconsistency, and poor patient experience.
solution: NutriLab provides a complete clinic management platform with patient registration, appointment scheduling, nutrition assessment tools, meal planning, PDF prescriptions, QR verification, and multi-role access.
features: Role-based access (Owner, Admin, Nutritionist, Receptionist, Finance, Patient)
architecture: Multi-tenant SaaS architecture with role-based access, secure patient data handling, and modular feature design for healthcare compliance.
challenges: Designing a data model that handles complex healthcare relationships
Implementing secure multi-tenant access with fine-grained permissions
Building PDF generation with dynamic content and professional formatting
engineeringDecisions: Multi-tenant architecture for scalability across clinics
Role-based access designed from day one
Modular feature design for future extensibility
lessonsLearned: Healthcare software demands rigorous data security
Multi-role systems require careful permission design
PDF generation requires significant engineering effort for quality output

name: FitFlow
overview: FitFlow is a modern desktop Gym Management Software developed by Forgeo. It provides gym owners with a fast, reliable, and easy-to-use desktop application for managing daily operations.
mission: Provide gym owners with a fast, reliable, and easy-to-use desktop application for managing daily operations.
problem: Gym owners struggle with managing memberships, attendance, billing, and trainer schedules using manual processes or expensive cloud-based solutions that require constant internet connectivity.
solution: FitFlow is a desktop application built with Electron that works reliably offline, provides complete gym management capabilities, and offers future cloud synchronization.
architecture: Enterprise desktop architecture with offline-first design, local SQLite database via Prisma, and Electron shell for cross-platform compatibility.
challenges: Designing an offline-first architecture that syncs seamlessly
Building a desktop UI that feels native and responsive
Managing local database migrations across distributed installations
engineeringDecisions: SQLite + Prisma for reliable local data storage
Offline-first design for gyms with unreliable internet
Future cloud sync designed as an optional layer
lessonsLearned: Desktop applications require different UX patterns than web apps
Offline-first design adds complexity but provides reliability
Electron + Prisma + SQLite is a powerful stack for desktop apps
